blocks.html: September 18, 2026 Bayview MSR Opportunity Master Fund, L.P. (together with its subsidiaries, the “MSR Fund”) To Our Valued Investors, The MSR Fund delivered a net return of +2.6% in the second quarter of 2026, bringing year-to-date net performance to +5.0%1, and ended the quarter with a NAV of approximately $13.5 billion and roughly $1.3 billion of uncalled capital. The MSR Fund called $200 million during the quarter and distributed approximately $295 million effective June 30, including voluntary withdrawals and approximately $68 million of quarterly yield distributions. Fundamental MSR performance remained in line with targeted returns, core cash flows were stable, sourcing was exceptionally strong, and the Guild Mortgage investment continued to perform ahead of initial underwriting expectations. Performance Review and Outlook MSR performance remained steady during the quarter, supported by stable fundamentals and moderate prepayment speeds. Sourcing was a highlight, as Bayview’s longstanding counterparty relationships, agency credibility, and transaction structuring capabilities supported significant bulk acquisition activity despite a competitive market. We continue to advance initiatives across the platform, driving earnings momentum and further expected upside from enhanced recapture, subservicing efficiencies, ancillary originations product growth, and Guild’s strong operating performance. We made progress this quarter on several initiatives designed to improve the MSR Fund's expense and financing profile. With respect to managing expenses, we continued transferring MSRs across the subservicers that optimize economics and performance, including through a renegotiated agreement with Mr. Cooper/Rocket, the migration of selected GNMA volume to M&T Bank, and the expansion of our servicing relationship with a newer technology-enabled platform for conventional portfolios. On the financing side, the MSR Fund priced approximately $520 million of unsecured debt in June across three-, five-, and seven-year tenors, which settled in July at spreads of 160 to 190 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. The issuance replaced $225 million of maturing notes, provided approximately $298 million of net incremental financing, and priced 172 to 202 basis points tighter in spread than the maturing debt, improving financing flexibility and bringing leverage closer to the MSR Fund's target range. Guild continued to perform ahead of our 2026 forecast and contributed approximately $91 million of P&L during the quarter, representing a quarterly ROE of +6.8%. We have already realized several benefits for the Guild platform, including the elimination of public-company costs, improved financing terms and associated reduction in interest expense, expansion of HELOC and non-QM offerings, and stronger originations execution via excess servicing retention. Guild has also retained approximately $11.8 billion of newly originated MSRs year to date, providing a recurring sourcing channel with strong recapture characteristics, while its positive duration and convexity have been providing a valuable offset to the MSR Fund’s broader delta hedging costs in a volatile rate environment. Several workstreams remain in development across Guild’s technology, servicing, and growth areas, including efforts to modernize loan origination technology with AI- supported front-end workflows, enhancing servicing technology to enable broader MSR Fund servicing cost efficiencies, and further expansion of Guild’s product suite. We expect these initiatives to translate into further upside in the quarters and years ahead. MSR Market Trends The second quarter was exceptionally strong from a sourcing perspective. Including Lakeview bulk and flow acquisitions, committed pipeline transactions, and MSRs retained by Guild, the MSR Fund acquired or committed to acquire approximately $1.03 billion of MSR market value. Aside from the fourth quarter of 2025 when the MSR Fund acquired Guild, this was the strongest sourcing quarter in the MSR Fund's history. Year-to-date sourcing has now reached approximately $1.7 billion of market value, the strongest first half on record, and the third quarter pipeline had already reached approximately $360 million at the time of writing. Bulk sourcing, including committed pipeline transactions, totaled approximately $722 million of market value, a quarterly record as the MSR Fund was the industry's largest buyer of agency MSR bulk portfolios.2 Notably, 73% of this quarter’s bulk purchases were GNMA MSRs. These assets require sophisticated credit modeling, liquidity management, servicing expertise, and EBO infrastructure, which limit the buyer universe and create a sourcing advantage for the MSR Fund. The MSR Fund also had success in directly negotiated opportunities where long-standing relationships, scale, and structuring flexibility allowed us to source assets at or above target returns, even in a competitive market. Recent acquisitions have reinforced this advantage, including transactions won based on Lakeview's ability to close quickly and accommodate bespoke servicing and recapture arrangements.

blocks.html: Flow sourcing remained steady at $204 million of market value in the second quarter, bringing year-to-date flow volume to $347 million of market value. Correspondent whole loan execution remains an attractive alternative to flow MSR sales for many originators, as that channel can imply MSR valuations above the MSR Fund's target levels. This has limited flow supply, but we believe that emerging earnings pressure across several large MSR owners may support increased flow volume in the coming quarters.

blocks.html: 1. Includes $83 million in market value of bulk deals committed to be purchased but not yet closed as of the end of the period. Prepayment Trends Prepayment speeds declined to 9.1 CPR in the second quarter from 10.2 CPR in the first quarter. Rate-term refinancing moderated to 2.5 CPR from 5.0 CPR as mortgage rates increased, while housing turnover increased seasonally to 5.3 CPR from 3.8 CPR as purchase and relocation activity accelerated into the summer. Cash-out refinancing remained modest at 1.4 CPR, as the majority of the portfolio remains materially out of the money to refinance.

blocks.html: Prepayment activity remained concentrated in the portfolio's recently originated, higher-coupon cohort. Loans originated after the post- COVID rate sell-off represented approximately 24% of portfolio UPB but accounted for 47% of total prepayments and 90% of rate-term refinance activity during the quarter. This remains the only cohort with meaningful rate-driven refinancing, but its observed behavior continues to track within our underwriting expectations.

blocks.html: 1. Data as of June 30, 2026. The MSR Fund’s recapture program remains a strategic priority as rate incentives evolve, and we continue to refine our program to retain borrowers and mitigate the economic impact of prepayments. Additionally, the MSR Fund’s second lien and HELOC originations reached approximately $578 million of UPB, generating approximately $47 million of net revenue during the first half of 2026. This was driven largely by second quarter volumes of $347 million of UPB, up approximately 50% from the first quarter. These junior lien originations help support borrower retention, drive ancillary earnings, and improve the MSR Fund’s convexity profile. Other Assets Excluding Guild, net exposure to non-MSR-related assets remained at approximately 10% of the MSR Fund's NAV at quarter-end. These investments contributed positively to performance during the second quarter. We continue to evaluate potential non-MSR investments based on their standalone risk-adjusted return potential and strategic value to the broader MSR platform.

blocks.note: (1) The year-to-date net return and the annualized net returns are calculated based upon the time-weighted rate of return of the net monthly returns during the applicable time period. The net monthly returns for the period starting from fund inception (September 2011) through March 2015 represent indicative net monthly returns of an investor paying a 2% management fee and 20% incentive fee. These returns are calculated based on the monthly aggregate gross fund return, including realized and unrealized gains and losses, and are net of total fund expenses adjusted for management and accrued incentive fees based upon an estimated 2% management fee and 20% incentive fee. From April 2015 forward, the net monthly returns are based on the actual monthly returns of a representative investor in the domestic feeder fund paying a 2% management fee and 20% incentive fee. An investor in the offshore feeder may have different returns based on various factors, including U.S and foreign income tax laws. The returns are calculated based upon beginning equity as adjusted for any capital activity for the month based on the applicable effective date. Actual management and incentive fees incurred by a limited partner may vary depending upon, among other things, the limited partner’s commitment size. Past performance is not a guarantee of future performance. No assurance can be given as to future performance. (2) Represents annualized time-weighted return since inception. An individual limited partner's annualized time-weighted return or IRR will vary from the rates disclosed based on different management fee and incentive fee arrangements.
